4. Proposed RAG pipeline
RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) allows the assistant to answer using approved documents retrieved at question
time. It is not a substitute for a transactional database, a clinical decision system or professional medical advice. Recommended ingestion flow
Stage What it does Implementation notes
1. Source intake Collect approved PDFs, text, FAQs, policy
documents and curated public-health material.

intake Collect approved PDFs, text, FAQs, policy
documents and curated public-health material. Track source, owner, publication date, version,
jurisdiction and permission to use. 2. Parsing and
cleaning
Extract text, tables and metadata; remove
boilerplate and duplicates. Keep page numbers and section headings for
citations; inspect OCR quality. 3. Chunking Split into meaningful passages with limited
overlap. Use heading-aware chunks; tune chunk size and
overlap using evaluation questions. 4.

Use heading-aware chunks; tune chunk size and
overlap using evaluation questions. 4. Embeddings Convert each chunk into a vector
representation. Choose an embedding model based on language,
cost, privacy and retrieval quality. 5. Storage and
indexing
Store text, metadata and vectors in a
searchable index. Use document-level access metadata and versioning;
never mix users' private records into a global corpus. 6. Retrieval Embed the question and retrieve relevant
passages.

records into a global corpus. 6. Retrieval Embed the question and retrieve relevant
passages. Apply user/role filters; consider hybrid keyword +
vector search and reranking. 7. Answer
generation
Give the LLM the question and selected
context. Require citations, uncertainty statements and refusal
when evidence is insufficient. 8. Evaluation and
feedback
Measure whether the right sources were
retrieved and answers are supported.

Evaluation and
feedback
Measure whether the right sources were
retrieved and answers are supported. Maintain a test set; log latency and errors without
unnecessarily logging sensitive content. Runtime question flow
User question → authenticate and identify role → validate question → retrieve permitted document chunks →
rank/filter context → generate grounded answer → attach source title/page/date → return answer and citations →
record minimal operational telemetry.

attach source title/page/date → return answer and citations →
record minimal operational telemetry. RAG safety rules
l The assistant must say when the knowledge base does not contain enough evidence; it must not invent a diagnosis,
coverage promise or eligibility decision. l Treat retrieved documents as untrusted content. A document must never override system instructions or request
secrets. l Use source allowlists, version metadata and review/approval before publishing health content.

l Use source allowlists, version metadata and review/approval before publishing health content. l Separate public knowledge retrieval from private patient-specific records. Private records require authorization and
strict per-user filtering. l Do not use RAG to diagnose, prescribe, triage emergencies or make final insurance decisions. Provide emergency
signposting and professional-care guidance where appropriate.
